memory_candidates.content: To scope a repo-wide housekeeping script that iterates every extension under a fixed directory (e.g. generate-context-line-counts.sh walking $EXT_DIR/*/index-entries.json) to just ONE extension, without a built-in per-extension flag, override the script's EXT_DIR env var to a throwaway temp directory containing a single symlink to the target extension (e.g. ln -s $(pwd)/agent-system/extensions/books /tmp/scope-dir/books). This avoids touching every other extension's files when only one extension's drift should be corrected -- critical when another concurrent task owns those other extensions' territory.

validate-no-task-references.sh (the PreToolUse Edit/Write hook enforcing no-task-references-in-deliverables.md) scans only the new_string/content passed to the tool call, never the whole file on disk. A file-top task-ref-ok:begin/:end exemption block opened at the start of the file does NOT cover a later mid-file Edit's own new_string, even though both land in the same already-exempted region once written. Any mid-file insertion carrying task-N-shaped fixture text (commit-subject examples, etc.) needs its own self-contained task-ref-ok:begin/:end pair inside that same Edit call's new_string, not reliance on an earlier marker elsewhere in the file.

When a shell script or test fixture must match a specific multibyte Unicode character extracted from an external reference file (e.g. an arrow U+2192 or em dash U+2014 inside another repository's markdown), embed it via an ANSI-C-quoted byte escape ($'\xe2\x86\x92') or a printf '\xHH\xHH\xHH' call rather than typing/pasting the literal character through an editing tool. This guarantees byte-for-byte correctness and is immune to the tool pipeline silently rendering an ASCII look-alike (a plain '-' for '--', a plain '>' sequence for an arrow) that would make the intended regex or string match silently fail.
